events.title: Mark Antony wins a final cavalry battle against Octavian
events.description: Mark Antony won a final cavalry battle against Octavian at Alexandria, but his infantry was defeated, and the next day his fleet and troops began to desert. Antony and Cleopatra took their own lives after Octavian's renewed invasion in early August.

events.title: Caliph al-Mansur founds Baghdad
events.description: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur laid the foundations of his Round City on the Tigris, naming it Madinat al-Salam, the City of Peace. Baghdad became a great centre of learning and trade.
events.html: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur laid the foundations of his Round City on the Tigris, naming it Madinat al-Salam, the City of Peace. Baghdad became a great centre of learning and trade.

events.title: Hussites kill seven councillors in the First Defenestration of Prague
events.description: In the first of the three Defenestrations of Prague, a crowd of radical Hussites, followers of the Czech reformer Jan Hus, threw members of the city council from a window, killing seven.
events.html: In the first of the three Defenestrations of Prague, a crowd of radical Hussites, followers of the Czech reformer Jan Hus, threw members of the city council from a window, killing seven.

events.title: Virginia's General Assembly meets for the first time
events.description: Elected burgesses met with the governor and council in the church at Jamestown. It was the first representative legislature in English America, the root of later colonial assemblies.
events.html: Elected burgesses met with the governor and council in the church at Jamestown. It was the first representative legislature in English America, the root of later colonial assemblies.

events.title: Scottish Covenanters under the Earl of Leven besiege Hereford
events.description: A Scottish Covenanter army under Alexander Leslie, Earl of Leven, laid siege to Hereford, one of the remaining Royalist strongholds of the English Civil War. The siege lasted until 4 September.
events.html: A Scottish Covenanter army under Alexander Leslie, Earl of Leven, laid siege to Hereford, one of the remaining Royalist strongholds of the English Civil War. The siege lasted until 4 September.

events.title: Baltimore is founded in Maryland
events.description: The Maryland legislature authorised a new town on the Patapsco River. Baltimore grew into a major Atlantic port; its defence in 1814 inspired 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.
events.html: The Maryland legislature authorised a new town on the Patapsco River. Baltimore grew into a major Atlantic port; its defence in 1814 inspired 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

events.title: German saboteurs blow up the Black Tom munitions depot
events.description: German agents set off explosions at the Black Tom depot in New York Harbor, destroying munitions bound for the Allies. The blast shattered windows across Manhattan and damaged the Statue of Liberty.

events.title: Lyndon Johnson signs Medicare and Medicaid into law
events.description: Johnson signed the Social Security Amendments in Independence, Missouri, with Harry Truman beside him. Medicare and Medicaid brought health insurance to millions of older and poorer Americans.
